text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Early Caspian oil may start flowing from Baku to Russia's export outlet in Novorosiisk along the pipeline passing through Chechnya before this autumn, said Sergei Kiriyenko, deputy Energy and Fuel Minister.

- The government is expected to sign a decree on allowing authorised commercial banks to export their gold reserves. The government has recently liberalised the gold market allowing citizens to buy gold and silver bars through commercial banks.

- The director general of the Ural Magnitogorsk Metallurgic Combine, Anatoly Starikov, was removed from his post on July 3. The paper said Starikov had opposed a plan by Inkombank to buy shares issued to raise investments for the combine's technical reconstruction.
- The Federal Arbitration Court of the Moscow region ruled that Purneftegaz, the main production unit of the state-owned Rosneft, should be returned to oil major Sidanko.

- Regional governors expressing support for the governor of the Far East Primorsky Krai, who has been summoned to Moscow in connection with strong social disturbances in the region, are worried about their own positions vis a vis the government.

- The government is planning to tighten controls over the process of auctioning off stakes in Russia's leading oil producers. A draft decree envisages some temporary restrictions on the rights of the investors.
- Russia's biggest oil producer LUKoil and Rosneft signed a deal with Azerbaijan on commecial principles to explore and develop the Kyapaz oil deposit in the Azeri section of the Caspian Sea.
- The government is planning to issue bonds to restructure Gazprom's debts to the state budget which have reached about 70 trillion roubles.
- Contract killers continue to pick off Russian businessmen, says the paper, referring to the murder of a local businessman in the Moscow region on Thursday.
- The Russian government decided to strip Ingushetia, a caucasian republic which boardes Chechnya, of its status as a free economic zone, saying it was inexpedient.
- The activities of 9,000 organised criminal groups, involving about 150,000 people, are being monitored by Russia's Interior Ministry, says minister Anatoly Kulikov.
- While Russians are struggling to survive on the Mir space station, the Americans are planning to occupy Mars.
- Moscow police are planning to invite psychologists and priests to deal with a growing number of suicides among local police officers, which has reached 13 for the last six months.
